ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r4.claim: Addressing his father as yā abati is a tactful appeal through their kinship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r4.anchor: وفي قوله يا أبت تلطف واستدعاء بالنسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r5.speaker: ابن عامر، الأعرج، أبو جعفر، هارون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r5.claim: Some read yā abati with an open tāʾ, which Harun criticized; the reading was discussed in Surat Yusuf. Abd Allah's codex has wā abati, with wāw instead of yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والأعرج وأبو جعفر يا أبت بفتح التاء وقد لحن هارون هذه القراءة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari praises Abraham's gentle sequence and considerate language in advising a father deeply mistaken in idol worship, emphasizing courtesy, kindness, and good character.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p267/r6.anchor: كيف رتب الكلام معه في أحسن اتساق وساقه أرشق مساق مع استعمال المجاملة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a report that God told Abraham to keep good character even with unbelievers; al-Zamakhshari adds extensive exhortatory material that the author omits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r1.anchor: حدث أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r2.claim: Mā lā yasmaʿ is likely a relative clause, though it can be an indefinite noun with description; the point is that idols lack hearing and sight without specifying an object. Shayʾan may be a verbal noun or object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p268/r2.anchor: الظاهر أنها موصولة، وجوزوا أن تكون نكرة موصوفة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r2.claim: The idolatrous submission is irrational: a maker possessing knowledge and power bows to a product that lacks both, as Abraham also says idols cannot hear, see, or help.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r2.anchor: وكيف لا يظهر هذا الضلال وهو عبادة وتذلل عبودي من صانع فيه آثار العلم والمقدرة لمصنوعه الذي يفقد العلم والقدرة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r3.claim: The verse’s short question summarizes several arguments Abraham made against idols, including their being human-made and lacking the qualities of lordship.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#12/r3.anchor: من الحجاج وإن كان بمنزلة التلخيص لعدة احتجاجات واجه بها ابراهيم عليه السلام أباه وقومه

TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.claim: By using the language of rational beings for what he does not love, Abraham suggests that objects without awareness or reason cannot merit lordship, as in his questions about idols’ hearing, benefit, and harm.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.anchor: وكأنه للإشارة إلى أن غير أولي الشعور والعقل لا يستحق الربوبية من رأس

TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.claim: The sequence suggests Abraham stayed with the star hypothesis until he saw it set; had he known it would set, he could have refuted its lordship as directly as he refuted idols.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.anchor: فإن فيه إشعارا بأنه عليه السلام مكث بانيا على كون الكوكب ربا حتى شاهد غروبه

BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r1.claim: The time phrase is an inclusion replacing Abraham’s name, and the address to his father Azar begins gently and makes the appeal easy to accept.
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r1.anchor: بدل من إبراهيم بدل الاشتمال لأن الأحيان مشتملة على ما فيها

BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r2.claim: In yā abati, tā substitutes for the possessive yāʾ, so it is not combined with it or a following alif.
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r2.anchor: فإن التاء عوض عن ياء الإضافة ولذلك لا يجتمعان

BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p258#2/r3.claim: Idols cannot hear worshippers’ praise or see their submission, benefit them, or avert harm; mā refers to images and statues.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r1.claim: The particle idh has been attached to Abraham as an appositional substitute, but objections say an uncoordinated substitute is unnatural and idh is usually indeclinable; other proposals attach it to kāna, prophet, or ṣiddīq, each with grammatical or contextual problems.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r1.anchor: وتعقبه صاحب الفرائد بأن الأعتراض بين البدل والمبدل منه بدون الواو بعيد عن الطبع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r2.claim: The best account makes idh an appositional substitute of inclusion for Abraham; attaching remembrance to times rather than events has been explained elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r2.anchor: والذي يقتضيه السياق ويشهد به الذوق البدلية وهو بدل اشتمال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r3.claim: Yā abati means ‘my father’: tāʾ replaces the possessive yāʾ, which is not normally combined with it except rarely; the added alif has competing grammatical explanations.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r3.anchor: يا أبت ( أي يا أبي فان التاء عوض من ياء الأضافه ولذلك لايجمع بينهما إلا شذوذا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r4.speaker: ابن عامر؛ الأعرج؛ أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Aʿraj, and Abū Jaʿfar read the vocative with fatḥa on tāʾ; Hārūn calls it incorrect, but the author says it is valid. ʿAbd Allāh's codex has wāw instead of yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والأعرج وابو جعفر ( يا أبت ) بفتح التاء وزعم هارون أن ذلك لحن والحق خلافه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r5.claim: Abraham uses the affectionate vocative to soften his appeal.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r6.speaker: أنس؛ أبو نعيم؛ الديلمي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r6.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says a child should address his father as Abraham addressed his—‘my father’—and not call him by name; this appears to imply biological fatherhood, though many hold that Abraham's addressee was his uncle and ‘father’ figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r6.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم والدليمي عن انس مرفوعا حق الوالد على ولده أن لا يسميه إلا بما سمى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r7.claim: ‘What you worship’ means an object that cannot hear your praise and appeals or cannot see your humility; alternatively, it cannot hear or see any sensible thing at all. Mā may be relative or an indefinite described noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96/r7.anchor: ثناءك عليه عند عبادتك له وجؤارك اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r1.claim: ‘It cannot avail you anything’ means it cannot bring benefit; shayʾan may be a direct object or an accusative verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r1.anchor: من الأشياء أو شيئا من الأغناء فهو نصب على المفعولية أتو المصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r2.claim: Abraham's argument models the finest method and manners: he asks for the reason behind worshiping something any rational person despises, avoiding a provocation to stubbornness while showing that worship belongs only to the self-sufficient creator and judge.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r2.anchor: ولقد سلك عليه السلام في دعوته أحسن منهاج واحتج عليه أبد احتجاج بحسن أدب وخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r3.claim: A rational person should act for a sound reason; even a living, perceptive being capable of benefit and harm would be dependent and unfit for worship, much less a lifeless manufactured idol.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p96#2/r3.anchor: والشيئ لو كان حيا مميزا سميعا بصيرا قادرا على النفع والضر لكن كان ممكنا لاستنكف ذو العقل السليم عن عبادته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r6.claim: Abraham's gentle invitation to his father teaches kindness in calling people to truth, especially when enjoining right and forbidding wrong among relatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r6.anchor: فيه من لطف الدعوة إلى اتباع الحق والارشاد اليه مالا يخفى وهذا مطلوب في الأمر بالمعروف والنهى عن المنكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r1.claim: Abraham's father is identified as Azar, who worshipped idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r1.anchor: {إذ قال} إبراهيم {لأبيه} آزر وهو يعبد الأصنام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r2.claim: Abraham says idols cannot hear sounds, see anything, or provide any benefit or sufficiency.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r2.anchor: {يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع} صوتا {ولا يبصر} شيئا {ولا يغني عنك} أي لا يكفيك

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r1.claim: “When” can modify Abraham or his earlier description, or attach to “was,” with an intervening parenthesis; the vocative ta replaces possessive ya, and repetition conveys tenderness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r1.anchor: { إذ قال } بدل من { إبراهيم } وما بينهما اعتراض

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r2.claim: The idols cannot perceive their worshipper, hear or see him, or bring benefit or avert harm. Abraham argues gently for worship of the self-sufficient creator alone; even contingent angels and prophets are not worthy of worship, much less inanimate idols.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r2.anchor: لا تحق إلا لمن له الاستغناء التام والإنعام العام

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r3.claim: Sound reason requires purposeful action; Abraham invites his father to follow him toward the straight path because he has received knowledge his father lacks.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:42/r3.anchor: فكيف إذا كان جمادا لا يسمع ولا يبصر

QASHANI:19:42-43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:42-43/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:42-43/r1.claim: Worship of anything besides God means seeking created things and attributing causal power to them; they truly provide no benefit because they have no effect.
QASHANI:19:42-43/r1.anchor: مما سوى الله من الأكوان التي تطلبها وتنسب التأثير إليها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r2.claim: Abraham addresses his father tenderly in every sentence, using courtesy, gentleness, and loving concern while guiding him away from idols.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r3.claim: The question is a tactful way to expose the futility of worshipping what cannot hear or see the worshipper's service or answer his call, now or later.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r3.anchor: المجاملة , واللطف والرفق واللين والأدب الجميل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r4.claim: Even a blind and deaf being might help by speech or otherwise, but idols cannot benefit or deserve worship; a worshipped object should not be inferior to its worshipper.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p536/r4.anchor: لن يكون المعبود دون العابد أصلا

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r1.claim: The deity must possess hearing and sight perfectly, without deficiency; the same standard applies to power over benefit and harm.
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r1.anchor: على استحقاق المعبود الوصف بالسمع والبصر على الكمال دون نقصان

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r2.claim: No created being can originate or create; attaching the heart to a creature or imagining even a sliver of independent efficacy resembles idol worship.
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r2.anchor: كل الخلق لا تصلح قدرة واحد منهم للإبداع والإحداث

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r6.claim: Abraham showed every form of compassion, but repeated counsel did not help his father because later effort cannot undo a prior decree of exclusion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r6.anchor: لم يغادر الخليل شيئا من الشفقة على أبيه ، ولم ينفعه جميل وعظه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r3.claim: Abraham’s rebuke to his father came by revelation so he could convey the invalidity of idol worship to his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r3.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن قوله لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر إنما كان عن وحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r5.claim: The temporal clause “when he said to his father” is an appositive specifying Abraham, and its time is singled out as especially worthy of remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r5.anchor: اذكر إبراهيم زمان قوله لأبيه فإن ذلك الوقت أجدر أوقات إبراهيم بأن يذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r6.claim: Abraham’s father was Āzar, previously identified in the Qur’an.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r7.claim: The added vocative summons the father’s attention despite his physical presence; Abraham begins with sensory evidence, then addresses resistance to taking advice from a son.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r7.anchor: وافتتح إبراهيم خطابه أباه بندائه مع أن الحضرة مغنية عن النداء قصدا لإحضار سمعه وذهنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr’s grandfather explains that the question leads the father to see he cannot justify worshipping what cannot hear or see; the uselessness argument follows, then Abraham anticipates the father’s resistance to a younger adviser.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r8.anchor: علم إبراهيم أن في طبع أهل الجهالة تحقيرهم للصغير كيفما بلغ حاله في الحذق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r9.claim: The grandfather’s account traces the appeal from sensory evidence and uselessness to the son’s limited knowledge, then Satan’s influence, and finally a hypothetical warning that idols cannot punish desertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p112/r9.anchor: فلما قضى حق ذلك انتقل إلى تنبيهه على أن ما هو فيه أثر من وساوس الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r1.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r1.claim: A couplet attributed to ʿAlī says that if astrologer and physician are right about no resurrection, the speaker loses nothing; if he is right, their loss is theirs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r1.anchor: زعم المنجم والطبيب كلاهمالا تحشر الأجسام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers the literal question analysis, following al-Kashshāf: the question indirectly denies any valid reason for idol worship and challenges the father to supply one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r3.anchor: الوجه ما بني عليه من أن الاستفهام مستعمل في حقيقته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r4.claim: The question is a rhetorical double entendre that conveys the father’s inability to provide the requested reason for worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r4.anchor: فهو كناية عن التعجيز عن إبداء المسؤول عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r5.claim: Yā abati derives from abī: the speaker’s yā is replaced irregularly by tāʾ in vocative use with father or mother, perhaps preserving an old Arabic form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r5.anchor: حذفوا ياء المتكلم وعوضوا عنها تاء تعويضا على غير قياس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r6.claim: Sībawayhi says the tāʾ becomes hāʾ in pause; al-Farrāʾ says it remains tāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r6.anchor: أن التاء تصير في الوقف هاء ، وخالفه الفراء فقال : ببقائها في الوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r7.claim: Most readers use kasra on tāʾ; Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar read it with fatḥa and no following alif, as if an alif after open vocative yāʾ were dropped.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر : ( يأبت ) بفتح التاء دون ألف بعدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r6.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r6.claim: Sibawayh treats the tāʾ in yā abati as replacing the possessive yāʾ and pauses on it as hāʾ; al-Farraʾ says the possessive yāʾ remains implicit and pause retains tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r6.anchor: فمذهب سيبويه أنها عوض من ياء الإضافة والوقوف عنده عليها بالهاء، ومذهب الفراء أن يوقف عليها بالتاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r7.claim: Most readers kasra the tāʾ; Ibn Masud's codex has wāw for the vocative, and Ibn Amir, al-Aʿraj, and Abu Jaʿfar read fatḥa as if deleting the alif of yā abātā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r7.anchor: وجمهور القراء على كسر التاء، وفي مصحف ابن مسعود «وا أبت» بواو للنداء، وقرأ ابن عامر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r8.speaker: هارون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r8.claim: Harun faulted the fatḥa reading, though another explanation treats the tāʾ as an inserted vocative marker like that in yā Ṭalḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p17#3/r8.anchor: ووجه آخر أن تكون التاء المقحمة كالتي في قوله يا طلحة وفي هذا نظر وقد لحن هارون هذه القراءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r1.claim: The object that neither hears nor sees is an idol; even perceptive beings such as angels would not thereby become worthy of worship, but the wording exposes idolatry's absurdity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r1.anchor: ، هو الصنم ولو سمع وأبصر كما هي حالة الملائكة وغيرهم ممن عبد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p236#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p236#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p236#2/r1.claim: What the idols cannot avail against is harm: they cannot ward it off from you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p236#2/r1.anchor: ولا يغني عنك شيئا أي لا يدفع عنك ضرا

SULAMI:v1p427/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p427/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p427/r1.claim: Do not rely on one who cannot hear your prayer, see your state, or meet any of your needs.
SULAMI:v1p427/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : لم تعتمد من لا يسمع دعائك ، ولا يبصر حالك ، ولا يكفيك شيئا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to recount Abraham to idol-worshipping people who claim his religious way; Abraham was a truthful prophet and gently challenged his father about powerless idols.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r1.anchor: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم واتله على قومك، هؤلاء الذين يعبدون الأصنام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r2.claim: The idols cannot hear, see, benefit their worshippers, or protect them from harm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p234#2/r2.anchor: أي: لا ينفعك ولا يدفع عنك ضررا.

JISHUMI:v6p4562/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r1.claim: These readers use fatḥa on the tāʾ in يا أبت throughout the Qur'an; the others use kasra.
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو جعفر [(ياأبت)] بفتح التاء في جميع القرآن

JISHUMI:v6p4562/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r2.claim: The tāʾ intensifies the possessive address; kasra seeks the possessive yāʾ and the stop retains tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r2.anchor: وإنما دخلت التاء في يا أبت للمبالغة في تحقيق الإضافة

JISHUMI:v6p4562/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r4.claim: Another analysis makes tāʾ replace the possessive yāʾ; fatḥa can represent يا أبتاه.
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r4.anchor: وقيل: التاء عوض من ياء الإضافة

JISHUMI:v6p4562/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r14.claim: Abraham addresses his father Āzar, who was an unbeliever.

JISHUMI:v6p4562/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r15.claim: Worship may mean worship, supplication, submission, or obedience; the objects may be idols or all celestial bodies and other things his people worshipped.
JISHUMI:v6p4562/r15.anchor: وقيل: أراد الأصنام، عن أكثر المفسرين

JISHUMI:v6p4564/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4564/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4564/r1.claim: Only a benefactor possessing original blessings—God, powerful, knowing, living, eternal—deserves worship; idols lack these attributes.
JISHUMI:v6p4564/r1.anchor: العبادة يستحقها المنعم بأصول النعم وهو الإله القادر العالم الحي القديم

JISHUMI:v6p4566/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r4.claim: Abraham's father was an unbeliever, as other Qur'anic verses say, so the plain meaning should not be displaced by figurative reinterpretation.
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن أبا إبراهيم كان كافرا، وقد ذكر في آي القرآن

JISHUMI:v6p4566/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r5.claim: Worship and following are acts of human agents, contradicting the opponents' doctrine about created acts.
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r5.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة والاتباع فعل العبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r1.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r1.claim: A prophetic report says God told Abraham, His close friend, to perfect his manners even toward unbelievers, promising him shelter beneath the Throne and nearness to God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r2.claim: Abraham first asks why his father worships, to awaken him to the grave persistence and excess of his error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r2.anchor: طلب منبه على تماديه ، موقظ لإفراطه وتناهيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r3.claim: Even a living, discerning, hearing, seeing, powerful created being is not fit for worship or lordship, even if an angel or prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r3.anchor: لاستخف عقل من أهله للعبادة ووصفه بالربوبية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r4.claim: Worship is the highest veneration and belongs only to the ultimate benefactor, creator, provider, life-giver, death-giver, rewarder, and punisher.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r4.anchor: وذلك أن العبادة هي غاية التعظيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r5.claim: Worship directed elsewhere is injustice, defiance, error, disbelief, and departure from clear truth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r5.anchor: لم يكن إلا ظلما وعتوا وغيا وكفرا وجحودا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r6.claim: An inert idol plainly cannot hear praise, see worship, avert harm, or meet a need.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r6.anchor: فلا يسمع يا عابده ذكرك له وثناءك عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r12.claim: Each of Abraham's four counsels begins yā-abati as a plea for closeness and compassion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r12.anchor: صدر كل نصيحة من النصائح الأربع بقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r13.claim: In mā lā yasmaʿ and mā lam ya'tika, mā may be relative or descriptive; the object of 'hears' and 'sees' is omitted and not intended.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r14.claim: Shayʾan can be an accusative verbal noun meaning any benefit, with a parallel sense supplied for the preceding verbs.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r15.claim: Alternatively, shayʾan is a direct object, following the expression aghna ʿannī wajhak.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p21/r15.anchor: أن يكون مفعولا به من قولهم : أغن عني وجهك

MUQATIL:19:41-44/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:41-44/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:41-44/r2.claim: Ibrahim asks his father Azar why he worships idols that cannot hear or see and cannot benefit him in the Hereafter.
MUQATIL:19:41-44/r2.anchor: ولا يغني عنك شيئا } [آية: 42] في الآخرة.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r1.claim: The time clause may attach to كان or to صديقا نبيا, describing Abraham as gathering the traits of the truthful and prophets when he addressed his father.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r1.anchor: وجاز ان يتعلق إذ بكان أو بصديقا نبيا اى كان جامعا لخصائص الصديقين والانبياء حين خاطب أباه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r2.claim: God is the one who records the story in revelation; the command to remember it means the Messenger should recite and convey it to people.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r2.anchor: ان يتلو ذلك على الناس ويبلغه اياهم كقوله واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم وإلا فالله عزوعلا هو ذاكره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r3.claim: Ibn Amir reads the tāʾ in يا أبت with either kasrah or fatḥah; it substitutes for the possessive yāʾ, so one does not combine both.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r3.anchor: بكسر التاء وفتحها ابن عامر والتاء عوض من ياء الإضافه ولا يقال يا ابتي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r4.claim: The idols neither hear nor see anything; the object is omitted but can be supplied as شيء.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r4.anchor: المفعول فيهما منسي غير منوى ويجوز أن يقدر اى لا يسمع شيئا ولا يبصر شيئا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r5.claim: In لا يغني عنك شيئا, شيئا may be a cognate accusative meaning no benefit at all, or a direct object in an idiom meaning it cannot help you.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p38/r5.anchor: يحتمل ان يكون شيئا فى موضع المصدر اى شيئا من الاعناء

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r2.claim: Abraham’s father was Azar, as discussed earlier; Abraham asks why he worships idols that cannot hear, see, or benefit him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r2.anchor: لم تعبد } أي لأي شيء تعبد: { ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r1.claim: In “O my father,” the tāʾ substitutes for the possessive yāʾ; “O my father” with both would combine substitute and original, though an alif form also occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r1.anchor: التاء عوض عن ياء الإضافة ولا يقال يا أبتي لئلا يجمع بين العوض والمعوض عنه

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r2.claim: Abraham’s first argument is that idols lack three attributes that disqualify them from divinity; worship is ultimate reverence and belongs only to the giver of every blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r2.anchor: العبادة غاية التعظيم فلا يستحقها إلا من له غاية الانعام وهو الإله الذي منه أصول النعم

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r3.claim: An idol that cannot hear, see, or distinguish obedience from disobedience cannot be divine; a true God must know all things.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r3.anchor: إذا لم تسمع ولم تبصر ولم تميز من يطيعها عمن يعصيها فأي فائدة في عبادتها

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r4.claim: Prayer is the core of worship, so an idol that cannot hear petitions or see an approach yields no benefit from worship or ritual proximity.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r4.anchor: وثالثها : أن الدعاء مخ العبادة فالوثن إذا لم يسمع دعاء الداعي

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r5.claim: A hearing, seeing, harming, and benefiting human is better than an idol lacking these traits, so it is unfit for the better to worship the inferior.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r5.anchor: السامع المبصر الضار النافع أفضل ممن كان عاريا عن كل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r6.claim: If idols can neither harm nor benefit, worship offers no hoped-for gain and avoids no danger.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r6.anchor: إذا كانت لا تنفع ولا تضر فلا يرجى منها منفعة ولا يخاف من ضررها

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r7.claim: Idols cannot even protect themselves from breaking; Abraham’s ability to smash them shows there is no reason to trust them for protection.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r7.anchor: إذا كانت لا تحفظ أنفسها عن الكسر والإفساد على ما حكى الله تعالى عن إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r8.claim: The threefold description of idols implicitly contrasts them with God, who hears, answers prayer, sees, and fulfills needs.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r8.anchor: بل الإلهية ليست إلا لربي فإنه يسمع ويجيب دعوة الداعي ويبصر

RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r9.claim: “Why do you worship?” refers literally to worship of idols; the later “do not worship Satan” means obey, but that figurative use gives no reason to alter the first phrase.
RAZI-FULL:v21p191#2/r9.anchor: محمول على نفس العبادة وأما قوله في المقام الثالث

RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r2.claim: An objection proposes that Abraham’s father viewed idols as creators, planetary images, honored human intercessors, talismans tied to rare planetary conjunctions, or another excuse.
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r2.anchor: فإن قيل : إما أن يقال إن أبا إبراهيم كان يعتقد

RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r3.claim: If the father thought carved wood created the universe, that is manifest madness; if he believed in planets, intercession, or talismans, the stated argument does not directly disprove those doctrines.
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r3.anchor: من / أجلى العلوم الضرورية ، فالشاك فيه يكون فاقدا

RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r4.claim: Al-Razi answers that the father’s view sought benefit from talismans or planets, and Abraham showed no benefit in obeying idols and no harm in neglecting them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p192/r4.anchor: على سبيل الخاصية الحاصلة من الطلسمات

STUDYQURAN:19:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r1.claim: The verse opens Quranic accounts of Abraham confronting his father Azār and his people over idolatry.
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r1.anchor: one of several Quranic accounts of Abraham’s confrontation with his father, Azār

STUDYQURAN:19:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r2.claim: Abraham's argument is that worshipping an object unable to hear or see is irrational.
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r2.anchor: an argument against idolatry that is repeated in various ways throughout the Quran

STUDYQURAN:19:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r3.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r3.claim: Idols cannot distinguish worshippers from nonworshippers or hear their prayers, and worshipping something less capable than oneself is futile.
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r3.anchor: they can neither distinguish those who worship them from those who do not nor hear the supplications of their devotees

STUDYQURAN:19:42/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r4.claim: Some identify the objects of worship as simple idols; al-Rāzī instead suggests they represented powerful stars or revered people thought able to intercede with God.
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r4.anchor: they may have worshipped them as representatives of the stars

STUDYQURAN:19:42/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r5.speaker: Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r5.claim: To avail someone means to avert harm or bring benefit, neither of which idols can do.
STUDYQURAN:19:42/r5.anchor: they cannot prevent or avert harm or bring benefit

NAHHAS:v3p18/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p18/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p18/r2.claim: The pause on يا أبت may use hāʾ because it is a feminine ending; Ibn Kaysān permits stopping on tāʾ because it attaches to an inseparable element.
NAHHAS:v3p18/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الوقف 42 بالهاء لأنها هاء تأنيث وقال أبو الحسن

NAHHAS:v3p18/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p18/r3.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p18/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says عصي and عاصي have the same meaning.

TAB-FULL:v15p549/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p549/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p549/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī introduces Abraham, God's intimate friend, and recounts that he was truthful in speech, reports, and promises.
TAB-FULL:v15p549/r1.anchor: كان صديقا} [مريم: 41] يقول: كان من أهل الصدق في حديثه وأخباره ومواعيده لا يكذب

TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r1.claim: An idol cannot answer when called, see or assist its worshipper, or remove harm, unlike the Lord who can do these things.
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r1.anchor: الذي إذا دعوته سمع دعاءك، وإذا أحيط بك أبصرك فنصرك، وإذا نزل بك ضر دفع عنك.

TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r2.speaker: نحويو البصرة
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r2.claim: Basran grammarians treat the h in أبت as an added vocative form; in pause it is abah, while connected or possessive forms use the t, and they allow the shortened vocative ab.
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r2.anchor: فكان بعض نحويي أهل البصرة يقول: إذا وقفت عليها قلت: يا أبه، وهي هاء زيدت نحو قولك: يا أمه،

TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r3.speaker: نحويو الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r3.claim: Kufan grammarians say the h in abah/ummah is a pause marker that became common; when a possessive yā is sought, it is pronounced t in يا أبت.
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: الهاء مع أبه وأمه هاء وقف، كثرت في كلامهم حتى صارت كهاء التأنيث، وأدخلوا عليها الإضافة،

TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r4.speaker: نحويو الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r4.claim: With the lamentation alif, يا أبتا can pause with t or h; pausing in h is unusual except under an analysis like the cited shortened Arabic form.
TAB-FULL:v15p549#2/r4.anchor: ومن قال: يا أبتا، فإنه يقف عليها بالتاء، ويجوز بالهاء، فأما بالتاء، فلطلب ألف الندبة،

TABATABAI:19:41-43/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:41-43/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:41-43/r5.claim: Abraham’s rebuke gives two reasons idol worship is futile: idols lack awareness to receive worship and lack power to benefit or protect their worshippers.
TABATABAI:19:41-43/r5.anchor: أن عبادة الأصنام لغو باطل من وجهين أحدهما أن العبادة إظهار الخضوع وتمثيل التذلل

TABATABAI:19:43-44/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:43-44/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:43-44/r1.claim: The person Abraham addressed as “father” was, according to the author’s earlier discussion, his uncle, maternal grandfather, or stepfather, not his biological father.
TABATABAI:19:43-44/r1.anchor: لم يكن والده وإنما كان عمه أو جده لأمه أو زوج أمه بعد وفاة والده

TABATABAI:19:43-44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:43-44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:43-44/r2.claim: In vocative يا أبت, the tāʾ substitutes for the first-person yāʾ; this substitution is restricted to address.
TABATABAI:19:43-44/r2.anchor: أن التاء عوض من ياء المتكلم ومثله يا أمت ويختص التعويض بالنداء

TABRISI:19:41-44/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:41-44/r13.claim: The father is Āzar; idols cannot hear prayer, see worshippers, or help them in worldly matters.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r13.anchor: آزر { يا أبت } أي يا أبي

TABRISI:19:41-44/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:41-44/r14.claim: The tāʾ in yā abat intensifies possession; Ibrahim asks why his father worships what cannot benefit or harm him.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r14.anchor: ودخلت التاء للمبالغة في تحقيق الإضافة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p253#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p253#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p253#2/r1.claim: The vocative ending in يا أبت was discussed at the start of Joseph; Abraham rebukes his father for worshipping an idol without hearing or sight that can avert harm or help.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p253#2/r1.anchor: {لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر} يعني الصنم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:40-42/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:40-42/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:40-42/r3.claim: Abraham asks why his father worships what cannot hear prayer, see worship, or protect him from God's punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:40-42/r3.anchor: لم تعبد ما لا يسمع } الدعاء { ولا يبصر } العبادة { ولا يغني } ولا يدفع { عنك } من عذاب الله { شيئا }.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p226/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p226/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p226/r4.claim: Abraham's father worshipped idols that neither hear nor see nor benefit anyone.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.claim: Abraham repeatedly addressed his father Azar respectfully as my father despite his idolatry and threats; the passage shows a younger person may advise an elder and that true religious guidance comes from revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim, babası Âzer’e her sözünün başında “babacığım” diye hitap etmekte

SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r1.claim: إذ قال لأبيه may be an apposition of inclusion to إبراهيم, despite the intervening إن كان صديقا نبيا, as in the cited construction; an earlier parallel is إذ انتبذت.
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إذ قال لأبيه }: يجوز أن يكون بدلا من " إبراهيم " بدل اشتمال كما تقدم في

SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows إذ to depend on كان or on صديقا نبيا, meaning Abraham possessed the qualities of the truthful and prophets when he spoke to his father.
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن يتعلق " إذ " ب " كان " أو ب " صديقا نبيا " ،

SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa’ likewise allows the الظرف to be governed by صديقا نبيا or by its meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r3.anchor: ولذلك جوز أبو البقاء أن يعمل فيه { صديقا نبيا } أو معناه.

SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r4.claim: The Shaykh objects that the apposition parse requires إذ to inflect, that كان governing a time adverb is disputed, and that a compound phrase cannot jointly govern it.
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " الإعراب الأول - يعني البدلية - يقتضي تصرف " إذ " وهي لا تتصرف، والثاني فيه إعمال " كان " في الظرف وفيه خلاف،

SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r5.claim: The Shaykh also says صديقا is already modified, except under Kufan grammar, while making إذ depend on نبيا implies Abraham became a prophet at that very moment.
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r5.anchor: ولا جائز أن يكون معمولا ل " صديقا " لأنه قد وصف، إلا عند الكوفيين.

SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r6.claim: The author adopts al-Zamakhshari’s combined sense: Abraham had the qualities of truthful men and prophets when he addressed his father.
SAMIN-DURR:19:42/r6.anchor: قلت: العامل فيه ما لخصه أبو القاسم ونضده بحسن صناعته من مجموع اللفظين كما رأيت في قوله " أي: كان جامعا

ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r1.claim: In address the Arabs say يا أبة and يا أمة, but do not use أبتي or أمتي in ordinary reported speech; the pause form is يا أبه.
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r1.anchor: الوقف عليه يا أبه بالهاء، والعرب تقول في النداء يا أبة، ويا أمة ولا

ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r2.speaker: الخليل
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh compare يا أبة to vocatives such as يا عمة and يا خالة; the form can address a male or female.
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r2.anchor: وزعم الخليل وسيبويه أنه بمنزلة قولهم يا عمة ويا خالة، وأن أبة للمذكر والمؤنث

ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r3.claim: The dual أبوان shows that the mother shares in the term of parenthood; the cited Qur'anic wording is “his parents inherited him.”
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r3.anchor: والدليل على أن للأم حظا في الأبوة أنه يقال أبوان، قال الله عز وجل: (وورثه أبواه).

ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r4.claim: The form also parallels feminine-looking descriptors used for males, such as رجل ربعة and غلام يفعة.
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r4.anchor: وزعم أنه بمنزلة قولهم رجل ربعة، وغلام يفعة.

ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r5.speaker: الخليل
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r5.claim: The hāʾ in أبة replaces the possessive yāʾ of يا أبي or يا أمي; it occurs only in address because yāʾ is often dropped there.
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r5.anchor: وأن الهاء في أبة، عوض من ياء الإضافة من يا أبي ومن يا أمي

ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r6.claim: Possessive yāʾ may be omitted in vocative يا أب, but not in non-vocative قال أب when “my father” is intended.
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r6.anchor: تقول: يا أب لا تفعل، ولا تقل قال أب كذا وكذا تريد قال أبي.

ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r7.claim: Feminine forms can describe males, as in امرأة طالق وطاهر; نفس is feminine even when three persons are called ثلاثة أنفس.
ZAJJAJ:v3p331/r7.anchor: والمؤنث قد يوصف بالمذكر كقولهم امرأة طالق وطاهر، ويقال ثلاثة أنفس،

ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r1.claim: The objects that neither hear, see, nor benefit are idols.

ASAD-NOTES:19:41#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:41#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:41#n31/r1.claim: Abraham's appeal to his father continues the preceding discussion by presenting Jesus and Abraham alike as mortal servants of the one God.
ASAD-NOTES:19:41#n31/r1.anchor: connects with the preceding discourse, under the same aspect, on the true nature of Jesus as a mortal human being and a mere servant of the One and Only God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prophets' accounts show Christians that earlier prophets taught Muhammad's message, while warning Quraysh that Abraham's and Ishmael's religion differs from what they now follow; the Qur'an presents Abraham's true religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The real religion of Abraham (sws) is the one which the Qur’ān is presenting before them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The repeated address Father shows Abraham's compassionate, affectionate concern for his misguided father throughout the argument.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: shows how compassionately and affectionately he spoke to him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Jews
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Jews claim that Āzar was Abraham's paternal uncle rather than his father.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: not his paternal uncle, as claimed by the Jews.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The source says exegetes accepted the claim that Āzar was Abraham's uncle without much deliberation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This opinion has been accepted without much deliberation by our exegetes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi rejects the uncle identification and holds Āzar was Abraham's father; he says later Sabā’ī writers turned the claim into propaganda.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Āzar is the name of Abraham’s (sws) father and not his paternal uncle

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi says later Sabā’ī writers made propaganda from the uncle claim and notes that he had refuted the Torah's account earlier.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Later the Sab ā’ī’s have created a propaganda from it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham first argues that handmade idols cannot hear, see, or help, making idolatry foolish and contrary to intellect and human nature.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: clearly shows that it is blatant foolishness and has no relation to intellect and human nature.

QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#1/r1.claim: The standard kasra on tāʾ is treated as a stabilized vocative ending.
QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#1/r1.anchor: Kasra on tāʾ: standard reading (canonical); tāʾ with kasra as stabilized vocative ending

QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#2/r1.claim: The alternate canonical fatḥa may reflect an accusative-like ending or another vocalization tradition for the vocative tāʾ.
QIRAAT-ER:19:42:6#2/r1.anchor: Fatḥa on tāʾ: alternate canonical reading; fatḥa may reflect an accusative-like case ending

RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r1.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r1.claim: Some say one may invoke God without mastering the premises; Razi rejects this as weak, since Abraham condemned worship of one who neither hears nor sees, and an incapable deity would fall under that criticism.
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r1.anchor: ومن الناس من يقول : لا حاجة في هذا الذكر إلى العلم بهذه المقدمات

RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r2.claim: Razi uses Abraham's rebuke of his father in 19:42 to argue that God must be known as all-hearing, all-seeing, and powerful over all things.
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r2.anchor: لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r3.claim: A servant must know he cannot fully guard his interests: even knowing what is needed, he cannot acquire what is absent or preserve what is present unaided.
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r3.anchor: يعلم عجزه وقصوره عن رعاية مصالح نفسه على سبيل التمام

RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r4.claim: Certainty about these truths produces humility and brokenness, then inward petition and the spoken invocation for refuge.
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r4.anchor: إذا حصلت هذه العلوم في قلب العبد وصار مشاهدا لها متيقنا فيها وجب أن يحصل في قلبه تلك الحالة المسماة بالانكسار والخضوع

RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r5.claim: People are powerless in both knowledge and action, the two things issuing from them; Razi begins by demonstrating their dependence on God for knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r5.anchor: الصادر عن الإنسان إما العمل وإما العلم وهو في كلا البابين في الحقيقة في غاية العجز

RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r6.claim: Even rigorous thinkers may remain mistaken about one doubt throughout life until later scholars expose their error, showing that human reasoning needs divine aid.
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r6.anchor: كم رأينا من الأكياس المحققين بقوا في شبهة واحدة طول عمرهم ولم يعرفوا الجواب عنها

RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r7.claim: Since everyone seeks true religion and sound belief, unaided will would make all correct; the tiny number of right-guided people shows that only God's aid rescues from error.
RAZI-FULL:v1p62#2/r7.anchor: لو كان الأمر بحسب سعيه وإرادته لوجب كون الكل محقين صادقين

BURHAN:v2p322/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p322/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p322/r2.claim: Calls may also precede interrogative or declarative sentences; Abraham’s address to his father is an interrogative example.
BURHAN:v2p322/r2.anchor: وقد تجيء معه الجمل الاستفهامية والخبرية كقوله تعالى في الخبر ﴿ يا عباد لا خوف عليكم ﴾ 3 وفي الاستفهام ﴿ يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ﴾ 4

BURHAN:v2p250/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p250/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p250/r1.claim: The twenty-eighth address type is affectionate address, illustrated by Abraham’s gentle يا أبت, Luqman’s يا بني, and Aaron’s يا ابن أم.

BURHAN:v3p131/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p131/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p131/r2.claim: The author instead likens bewildered disbelievers to livestock hearing its herder call: they invoke things that cannot hear, see, or understand, with an ellipsis in the parable.
BURHAN:v3p131/r2.anchor: بل الناعق من الحيوان شبههم في تألهم وتأتيهم بما ينعق من الغنم بصاحبه

BURHAN:v3p176/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p176/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p176/r1.claim: The examples يحيي ويميت and Moses’ question about worshipping what neither hears nor sees omit objects because the point is God’s power to give life and death and the idol’s lack of senses.
BURHAN:v3p176/r1.anchor: والمراد أن الله تعالى له الإحياء والإماتة وأن إلههم ليس له سمع ولا بصر

ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.claim: A vocative can stand without a following command, introducing a statement such as people’s dependence on God or Abraham’s question to his father.
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r4.anchor: وقد لا تعقبها نحو ﴿ يا عباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ﴾ ﴿ يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله ﴾

ITQAN:v3p92/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.claim: An affectionate address appears in Abraham's gentle address to his father, Luqmān's address to his son, and Aaron's appeal to Moses; 20:94 is cited as an example.
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.anchor: الحادي والثلاثون خطاب التحبب نحو ﴿ يا أبت لم تعبد ﴾ ﴿ يا بني إنها إن تك ﴾

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r1.claim: Calling one person 'the man' can elevate him so completely that everyone else is excluded from the category; the wording treats their existence as absence.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r1.anchor: نزلت الوجود فيمن عدا المذكور منزلة العدم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r2.claim: A milder 'this is a man' can mean someone of full stature without denying that other people are men; 'this is something' can likewise mean merely countable or especially significant.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r2.anchor: هذا رجل تريد كامل من الرجال لا أن من عداه فليس برجل على الكمال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r3.claim: When opposed qualities differ in excellence, lack of the superior quality may be named by its opposite: life without knowledge is death, and unbeneficial sight or hearing is called blindness or deafness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r3.anchor: جعلت الحياة العارية من فضيلة العلم والقدرة موتا والبصر والسمع إذا لم ينتفع صاحبهما بما يسمع ويبصر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r4.claim: Calling someone deaf and blind in this usage means he gains nothing from what he hears or sees, as if he had neither faculty.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r4.anchor: وقيل للرجل هو أعمى أصم يراد أنه لا يستفيد شيئا مما يسمع ويبصر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r5.claim: In a qualified expression such as 'deaf to what offends, hearing otherwise,' both qualities coexist generally; deafness is limited to a class or circumstance, not asserted absolutely.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p60/r5.anchor: أصم عما ساءه سميع فتثبت له الصفتان معا على الجملة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r1.claim: Figurative action can lie in the act itself: someone escaping near-death is said to have been created anew because the near-death state is treated as nonexistence.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r1.anchor: هو إنما خلق الآن وإنما أنشىء اليوم وقد عدم ثم انشىء نشأة ثانية

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r2.claim: By contrast, saying spring made flowers uses a real act of making but figuratively attributes it to spring rather than to God, the true agent.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r2.anchor: الفعل واقع على النور حقيقة وهو مفعول مجهول على الصحة إلا أن حق الفعل فيه أن يثبت لله تعالى وقد تجوز بإثباته للربيع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r3.claim: In the Quranic phrase about reviving earth after its death, Jurjani says the metaphor lies in 'life' itself, since the intended referent is other than the earth, not in attributing the act.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r3.anchor: الحياة صفة للأرض في قوله تعالى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r4.claim: A thing cannot be called metaphorical or literal merely as something asserted: every assertion must belong to something, so those labels concern the content asserted or its attribution.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r4.anchor: استحال أن يوصف المثبت من حيث هو مثبت بأنه مجاز أو حقيقة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r5.claim: Derived verbs such as weaving, forging, embroidering, and painting name real processes; saying spring performs them is figurative in attributing the action, not in the action word.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r5.anchor: أتقول إذا قيل نسج الربيع وصاغ الربيع ووشى أن المجاز في مصادر هذه الأفعال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r6.claim: In 'the report pleased me,' pleasure is real, so the metaphor is the attribution that makes the report seem to cause it; this cannot be a lexical metaphor in the verb.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p326/r6.anchor: قولك سرني الخبر فإن السرور بحقيقته موجود والكلام مع ذلك مجاز

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r1.claim: Some compositions require the parts to be planned together, with meanings interwoven and later clauses strongly bound to earlier ones; their forms are varied rather than governed by one exhaustive rule.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r1.anchor: وأن يحتاج في الجملة إلى أن تضعها في النفس وضعا واحدا ، وأن يكون حالك فيها حال الباني

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r2.claim: One form pairs meanings across condition and result; al-Buḥturī’s paired love and estrangement clauses show the structure.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r2.anchor: فمن ذلك أن تزاوج بين معنيين في الشرط والجزاء معا كقول البحتري ، + الطويل + :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r3.claim: Another paired conditional makes a remembered kinship bring tears just as conflict brings bloodshed.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r3.anchor: إذا احتربت يوما ففاضت دماؤها تذكرت القربى ففاضت دموعها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r4.claim: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Quḍāʿī juxtaposes falling from high rank with a renewed rise, then prosperity with hardship followed by wealth.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r4.anchor: نوع منه آخر قول سليمان بن داود القضاعي ، + الوافر + :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r5.claim: Kathīr compares his pursuit of ʿAzza to seeking shade that disappears, while al-Buḥturī depicts time’s force against the weak as the strong’s attack.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r6.claim: The second half of Kathīr’s comparison completes the image of the cloud’s vanishing shade as the seeker settles beneath it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r6.anchor: لكالمرتجي ظل الغمامة كلما تبوأ منها للمقيل اضمحلت

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r7.claim: Al-Buḥturī’s oath introduces an image of time’s aggression against the weak by the powerful, another tightly paired construction.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r8.claim: Division followed by collection is especially elegant: Ḥassān first separates harm to enemies from benefit to allies, then gathers these traits under one inherited disposition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r8.anchor: ومنه التقسيم ، وخصوصا إذا قسمت ، ثم جمعت كقول حسان ، + البسيط + :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r9.claim: Ḥassān’s next line gathers the divided traits into a single disposition, strengthened by the statement that new traits are the worst.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r9.anchor: سجية تلك منهم غير محدثة إن الخلائق فاعلم شرها البدع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r10.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r10.claim: An unnamed poet first contrasts the listener’s hoped-for permanence with his own, then concludes that tomorrow will bring a change from both states.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r10.anchor: ومن ذلك ، وهو شيء في غاية الحسن ، قول القائل ، + البسيط + :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r11.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r11.claim: The ending جمع فيما قسم by saying both parties will experience a change tomorrow; its effect is heightened by the preceding statement that this thought brought peace.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p87/r11.anchor: قوله : ' سنستجد خلاف الحالتين غدا ' جمع فيما قسم لطيف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r1.claim: An object may be absent because the point is to assert the act itself as characteristic, without specifying something the act affects.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r1.anchor: فهذا قسم من خلو الفعل عن المفعول ، وهو أن لا يكون له مفعول يمكن النص عليه .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r2.claim: Saying he gives dinars specifies what he gives; it does not merely assert that he gives, so adding an object changes the focus.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r2.anchor: ألا ترى أنك إذا قلت : هو يعطي الدنانير ؛ كان المعنى على أنك قصدت أن تعلم السامع أن الدنانير تدخل في عطائه ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r3.claim: A second kind has a definite object understood from context: the conventional examples mean one lends an ear and lowers an eyelid.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r3.anchor: فمثال الجلي قولهم : أصغيت إليه : وهم يريدون أذني ، و : أغضيت عليه : والمعنى جفني .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r4.claim: Artful omission hides a specific known object so the speaker seems to assert the action alone, producing an additional rhetorical effect.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r4.anchor: وفي نفسك له مفعول مخصوص قد علم مكانه ؛ إما لجري ذكر أو دليل حال .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r5.claim: Al-Buḥturī’s line implicitly says that observers see al-Muʿtazz’s virtues and listeners hear their report; the omitted objects let the poet conceal the intended praise.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r6.claim: The poem praises al-Muʿtazz while alluding to al-Mustaʿīn: visible and audible virtues prove the former’s right to the caliphate and torment rivals who know it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p128/r6.anchor: وذاك أنه يمدح خليفة ، وهو المعتز ، ويعرض بخليفة وهو المستعين .

DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r3.claim: Ab can mean one’s actual father, as in Abraham’s address to his father and the references to Āzar and parents.
DAMGHANI:v1p13#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : الأب الوالد بعينة قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r1.claim: With a light bāʾ, ab means father; with a doubled bāʾ, it means pasture, as in fākihatan wa-abbā.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r1.anchor: الأب : بتخفيف الباء : الوالد . وبتشديدها : المرعى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r2.claim: The verb abba means to prepare to depart, with the forms abā, abābah, and abīban; al-Aʿshā supplies a poetic example.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r2.anchor: ويقال : أب الرجل إذا تهيأ للذهاب : أبا ، وأبابة ، وأبيبا : وأنشد للأعشى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r3.claim: The first Qur’anic sense is a near or direct father, illustrated by Abraham addressing his father and other family passages.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p111/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الأب ' بتخفيف الباء ' في القرآن على أربعة أوجه :

IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r1.claim: Abu Amr compares his generation with earlier scholars to small plants at the roots of tall palms, expressing their lesser stature.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r1.anchor: قال أبو عمرو إنما نحن فيمن مضى كبقل في أصول نخل طوال

IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r2.claim: Ibn Mujahid compares transmission criticism in readings with hadith criticism: reports may be accepted and widespread, rejected despite transmission, or corrected as mistakes by specialists.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r2.anchor: وأما الآثار التي رويت في الحروف فكالآثار التي رويت في الأحكام منها المجتمع عليه السائر المعروف ومنها المتروك المكروه عند الناس

IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r3.claim: He classifies reading reports as sound and widespread, sound but uncommon, rare dialect, weak in grammar though recited, obvious error, or subtle error discerned only by expert grammarians.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r3.anchor: كذلك ما روى من الآثار في حروف القرآن منها المعرب السائر الواضح ومنها المعرب الواضح غير السائر ومنها اللغة الشاذة القليلة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r4.claim: Only specialists in reports and legal rulings can properly evaluate disputed transmissions; persistence in an error may discredit a transmitter.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r4.anchor: وإنما ينتقد ذلك أهل العلم بالأخبار والحرام والحلال والأحكام وليس انتقاد ذلك إلى من لا يعرف الحديث

IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r5.claim: The regional readings of Mecca, Medina, Kufa, Basra, and Syria were received from predecessors and followed a locally established reader whose reading was accepted publicly and privately.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p48/r5.anchor: والقراءة التي عليها الناس بالمدينة ومكة والكوفة والبصرة والشام هي القراءة التي تلقوها عن أوليهم تلقيا

NASHR:v2p131/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p131/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p131/r1.claim: At ياأبت in Yūsuf, Maryam, al-Qaṣaṣ, and al-Ṣāffāt, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqūb stop with hāʾ; the rest stop with tāʾ as written.
NASHR:v2p131/r1.anchor: فوقف عليها بالهاء خلافا للرسم: ابن كثير وابن عامر، وأبو جعفر ويعقوب.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r1.claim: A deficient noun has a final weak radical after a short vowel; its final alif replaces yāʾ or wāw, which do not show ordinary case endings.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r2.claim: Forms such as معطى and مشترى are identified as deficient by comparison with regular patterns such as مخرج and معترك.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r3.claim: The forms مسلقى and مسلنقى follow سليقيته: a corresponding sound consonant would occur after a short vowel, revealing the weak radical.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r3.anchor: وذلك قولك مسلقى ومسلنقى والدليل على ذلك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r4.claim: When the sound-root counterpart is an adjective on أفعل with a verbal noun on فعل, weak-root forms such as أعشى, أعمى, and أقنى are deficient.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r4.anchor: وللأقرع به قرع وللأصلع به صلع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r5.claim: If a verb is فعل يفعل and its noun is فعل, its weak-root verbal noun is deficient; examples include هوى, ردى, صدى, لوى, كرى, and غوى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r5.anchor: فرق يفرق فرقا وهو فرق وبطر يبطر بطرا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r6.claim: The same inference applies when فعل يفعل has a sound-root noun on فعلان, as in عطشان and ظمآن; weak-root examples include طوى and صدى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r6.anchor: للعطشان عطش يعطش عطشا وهو عطشان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r7.claim: غرى has the anomalously extended form الغراء, compared also with الظماء; such exceptions are learned from usage.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r7.anchor: وقالوا غرى يغرى غرى وهو غر والغراء شاذ ممدود

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r8.claim: رضا also departs from its regular comparison with سخط; its vowel pattern cannot be generalized without attested usage.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r8.anchor: وقالوا رضى يرضى وهو راض وهو الرضا ونظيره سخط يسخط سخطا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r9.claim: The form بدا is likewise accepted from attestation, with حلب offered as its sound-root parallel; such forms cannot confidently be produced without hearing them.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r10.claim: Some short nouns such as قفا, رحى, and رجا البئر cannot be identified as deficient by analogy alone; hearing establishes their weak origin.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r10.anchor: فمن ذلك قفا ورحى ورجا البئر وأشباه ذلك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r11.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r11.claim: An extended noun has final yāʾ or wāw after an alif; analogy with sound-root forms can identify it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r11.anchor: وأما الممدود فكل شيء وقعت ياؤه أو واوه بعد ألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r12.claim: Verbal nouns from patterns such as استسقى, اشترى, and أعطى are extended because their final weak radical follows an alif, as in regular-root analogues.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r12.anchor: وذلك نحو الاستسقاء لأن استسقيت استفعلت مثل استخرجت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r13.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r13.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r13.claim: Forms such as الاحبنطاء and الاسلنقاء are extended by the same pattern: the weak radical would follow an alif if replaced by a sound consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r13.anchor: فكذلك جاءت الياء بعد ألف فإنما تجيء على مثال الاستفعال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r14.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r14.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r14.claim: Sound-related verbal nouns with initial ḍamma, such as العواء, الدعاء, and الزقاء, indicate an extended weak-root form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r14.anchor: ومما تعلم به أنه ممدود أن تجد المصدر مضموم الأول يكون للصوت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r15.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r15.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r15.claim: Al-Khalīl says speakers who shorten البكاء make it parallel to الحزن.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r15.anchor: وقال الخليل الذين قصروه جعلوه كالحزن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r16.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r16.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r16.claim: Action nouns such as النزاء follow the extended pattern, comparable to the regular-root القناص.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r16.anchor: نحو النزاء ونظيره من غير المعتل القناص

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r17.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r17.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r17.claim: A verbal noun with initial ḍamma is rarely deficient because the corresponding فعل pattern is seldom a verbal noun outside weak-root forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r17.anchor: لأن فعلا لا تكاد تراه مصدرا من غير بنات الياء والواو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r18.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r18.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r18.claim: Some extended forms are recognizable only by hearing, including السماء, الرشاء, الآلاء, and المقلاء.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r19.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r19.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r19.claim: A plural on أفعلة normally points to an extended singular, as with أقبية and أرشية; ندى وأندية is an exception.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r19.anchor: نحو أقبية واحدها قباء وأرشية واحدها رشاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r20.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r20.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالمقصوروالممدود)#648/r20.claim: Group nouns whose singular is on فعلة or فعلة are short, as in عروة/عرى and فرية/فرى.
